ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Low global contrast ratio; over 90% of the surface area is comprised of low-intensity (black/dark grey) pixels, with less than 10% high-intensity (white/light grey) localized anomalies.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant low-intensity contiguous field across both lobes. High-intensity circular blobs (diameter ~10-30 pixels) are scattered on the mid-right lobe and lower-left lobe. High-intensity linear streaks are mapped to the inner right lobe and lower-center region.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped central depression with a calculated angle of approximately 55 degrees and a bounding-box depth of approximately 120 pixels relative to the highest lobe peaks.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Medium-frequency serrations (peaks every 30-50 pixels) with a pixel-amplitude of 5-15 pixels along the upper continuous linear boundary, ending in high-amplitude irregular clusters at the distal tips.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bi-convex curve fitted to the upper edges of both lobes, transitioning to a jagged, irregular profile at the lateral extremities due to bio-encrustation.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Detection of 5 distinct high-contrast white ring-shaped clusters on the right lobe and 3 circular solid white spots on the left lobe, typical of parasitic attachment scars.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Two distinct unaligned linear pixel disruptions: a prominent V-shaped white scratch on the inner right lobe and multiple smaller vertical scratches on the lower left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Massive clusters of barnacles (biofouling) visible as dense, textured, high-contrast bulbous protrusions on the outer distal tips of both lobes.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique non-linear edge profile at the distal tips caused by heavy barnacle colonization, significantly deviating from the standard geometric sweep of the fluke lobes.
